newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds finish higher in thin market.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds finish higher in thin market.

text.p: Local Argentine bonds finished much higher Monday on the last trading day of the year as traders and analysts hoped for more gains in the coming year.
"For the short-term I continue to be bullish," said Roberto Costa Bourdieu, senior fixed income analyst at Banco Rio.
The market maintained its strong tone amid an absence of market players. The few players that were still squaring positions were on the buy side.
The dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 edged up $0.48 to 123.80, while in New York Argentina's FRB Brady bond due 2005 rose 1/8 to 87-5/8.

Analysts said the outlook for the first weeks of January was positive with the prospect of continued strong U.S. Treasuries and an expected large Argentine global bond issue lending a positive undertone.

"Within a stable international context, with less volatility in the U.S. bond market, the perspectives for domestic bonds continue to be positive," said analysts at consultancy Macroeconomica in an investor note.
In the money markets, call money rates rose to 8.05 percent from 8.0 percent.
Argentine financial markets are closed Tuesday and Wednesday for New Year holidays.
